observation: Architecture critique required 2 rounds: round-1 CRITICAL C1 (block→knowledge mapping not total over BlockHostKind — adapter had no rule for bet/task/artifact/agent/user-hosted blocks), plus 4 WARNINGs. Round-2 re-review found W5 (entity-ref→OpenTarget not total over EntityRef.kind — 'message' member had no mapping). Both totality holes were missed by the reconciliation pass in the initial plan because the plan checked route/type existence but not exhaustiveness of discriminated-union dispatch.

Scope BLOCKER mid-build: builder completed substrate tasks 1-7 but did NOT migrate live Conversations.tsx page — still rendered ThreadShell. Plan task 8 ('Wire Conversations.tsx') was ambiguous: never stated whether the deliverable was the story only or story + live page. Builder flagged a regression risk on protected inline-verdict behaviors. Founder resolved with policy ('desktop app, every change done completely') which triggered architecture amendment (§12, tasks 11-14) and a second build session.

Review round 1: CRITICAL ARCH-1 — betId hardcoded as '' in source-agnostic adapter; open-handler built /work/bet//review/:id (double-slash dead URL). Three review tests asserted around the defect (toContain('/work/bet') passes on a double-slash path; typeof betId === 'string' passes on ''). Fix required sourcing betId at page boundary and threading it through OpenTarget. The plan named ReviewPage as the destination but did not specify the betId wiring for the page-boundary seam.

Spec said 'Depends on: None' but AM1 functionally depends on AL3 (ReviewPage.handleSubmitVerdict is a no-op stub) and AM5 (open/routing contract). With inline verdict removed and AL3 not wired, no reachable approve path in merged product. Work-planning dependency declaration missed functional/sequencing dependencies; only listed technical build dependencies.

AC/design contradiction: validation scenario said 'verdict flow is unaffected' but locked design §5 explicitly removed inline Approve/Reject from the conversation. Architecture plan §12.9 reconciled this correctly but the AC wording was never updated. Code reviewer had to make an explicit ruling to avoid a false NOT DONE verdict. Should have been reconciled at plan or write-tests time.

Source-agnostic Part boundary enforced by a scoped no-restricted-imports ESLint rule banning Message/InlineRef/EntityRef/BlockRef/MentionRef named imports and thread*/harness path patterns in PartList.tsx+parts/**. Rule verified firing as error on a planted import during review. Correct tool (static property → lint rule, not a test). Directly enables the AM3 reuse contract.

Single onOpen routing seam (createOpenHandler) collapsed three callbacks into one, kept renderer router-free, and survived the scope-blocker amendment cleanly: pre-wired in session 1, consumed correctly in session 2. Story passes console.info noop; page passes real navigator. Clean separation, no rework.

Architecture critique caught C1 (block→knowledge totality) and W5 (entity-ref totality) before build. C1 fix reused the existing TS-exhaustive resolveHostRoute resolver — no new code, provably total. W5 fix stated the message-kind rule explicitly so builder had a documented decision. Both would have become builder improvisation without the critique gate.

ConversationSurface composes PartList — design story and production page run through the same renderer. Session-2 migration extended ConversationSurface to accept real props; story passes fixtures, page passes real data. Design/production drift is structurally impossible. The 'round-10 lore' anti-drift pattern worked as intended.

8 founder annotation rounds produced a single locked, unambiguous approved design before pipeline resumed. Architecture plan had unusually clear inputs — every load-bearing detail (identity model, author grouping, chip kinds, composer menu, review shape, session fold, routing contract) was settled. High design round count was appropriate for a primary-surface redesign.

Cost signal: 39 commits from concept to plan retirement. Build phase: session 1 (substrate, tasks 1-7+10) + architecture amendment (§12) + session 2 (migration, tasks 11-14) + 3 fix commits (review round 1) + docs. Rework commits: 4 (2 fix, 1 test tighten, 1 QuestionnairePart honest state). Architecture phase: 2 critique rounds + 1 W5 fold before any code. Two review rounds. Design phase (pre-pipeline): 8 annotation rounds.

Totality audit is a pattern worth adding to architecture-critique/SKILL.md as a required lens: for every discriminated-union dispatch in the plan, verify the plan states a rule for every member. C1 (BlockHostKind) and W5 (EntityRef.kind) were both caught by critique but required 2 rounds. A named 'Totality audit' lens in the critique skill would make this check systematic rather than critic-dependent.

Live-page migration scope must be explicit in architecture plans for surface redesigns. 'Wire Conversations.tsx' in a numbered task does not communicate whether the live page is in scope. For primary surfaces, the 'desktop app — every change done completely' policy is load-bearing context that should be stated in the plan, not resolved at build-time via a founder interrupt.

Functional + sequencing dependencies must be declared separately from build dependencies. 'Depends on: None' was technically correct (AM1 compiles without AL3 or AM5) but misleading about capability regression: removing inline verdict dispatch (correct per locked design) combined with AL3 no-op stub and AM5 unbuilt creates a window where approve is unreachable. Work-planning spec template needs a functional/sequencing dependencies field.
